title: Joshua Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Joshua chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Joshua Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Joshua Chapter 6.

questions.question: What was the state of Jericho when the children of Israel approached?
options: It was straitly shut up with no one going out or in
It was open and undefended
It was surrounded by water
It was abandoned
questions.correctAnswer: It was straitly shut up with no one going out or in
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:1 states that Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in.

questions.question: Who did the LORD say He had given into Joshua's hand?
options: Jericho, its king, and mighty men of valour
All the cities of Canaan
Egypt and its army
The Philistines
questions.correctAnswer: Jericho, its king, and mighty men of valour
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:2 says the LORD told Joshua He had given into his hand Jericho, the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour.

questions.question: How many days were the men of war to compass the city once each day?
options: Six days
Seven days
Three days
Ten days
questions.correctAnswer: Six days
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:3 commands to compass the city once every day for six days.

questions.question: How many priests bore trumpets before the ark of the covenant?
options: Seven priests
Three priests
Twelve priests
One priest
questions.correctAnswer: Seven priests
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:4 states that seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark.

questions.question: What were the priests to blow on the seventh day as they compassed the city seven times?
options: Trumpets of rams' horns
Silver trumpets
Flutes
Shofars made of other animals
questions.correctAnswer: Trumpets of rams' horns
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:4 says seven priests shall bear seven trumpets of rams' horns and blow them on the seventh day.

questions.question: What happened when the people heard the trumpet sound and shouted with a great shout?
options: The wall of the city fell down flat
The city gates opened on their own
The sun darkened
The priests stopped blowing trumpets
questions.correctAnswer: The wall of the city fell down flat
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:5 states that when the trumpet sounded and the people shouted, the wall fell down flat.

questions.question: Who did Joshua call to carry the ark of the covenant and the trumpets?
options: The priests
The mighty men of valour
The elders of Israel
The children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The priests
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:6 says Joshua called the priests and told them to take up the ark and bear trumpets before it.

questions.question: What did Joshua command the armed men to do as they compassed the city?
options: Pass on before the ark of the LORD
Stay behind the ark of the LORD
Hide inside the city
Blow trumpets
questions.correctAnswer: Pass on before the ark of the LORD
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:7 states Joshua told the armed men to pass on before the ark of the LORD while compassing the city.

questions.question: In what order did the priests, armed men, and ark move around the city?
options: Priests with trumpets first, then armed men, with the ark following
Ark first, then priests, then armed men
Armed men first, then ark, then priests
Priests last, with armed men and ark first
questions.correctAnswer: Priests with trumpets first, then armed men, with the ark following
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:8-9 describes the seven priests with trumpets going before the LORD, the armed men going before the priests, and the ark of the covenant following them.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua commanded the people to shout loudly as they compassed the city each day.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:10 commands the people not to shout or make any noise until Joshua tells them to shout.

questions.question: True or False: Seven priests with seven trumpets continuously blew the trumpets as they went before the ark.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:13 states the seven priests bearing seven trumpets went on continually blowing the trumpets before the ark of the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: The ark of the LORD compassed the city seven times each day for six days.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:14 clarifies they compassed the city once each day for six days, but seven times only on the seventh day.

questions.question: True or False: The city of Jericho was accursed and everything in it was devoted to destruction except Rahab and her family.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:17 says the city and all therein shall be accursed to the LORD, except Rahab and all that are with her in the house.

questions.question: What did Joshua command the people to do with the accursed things from Jericho?
options: Keep themselves from the accursed thing to avoid becoming accursed
Take them for themselves as spoils
Sell the accursed things to other nations
Ignore the accursed things completely
questions.correctAnswer: Keep themselves from the accursed thing to avoid becoming accursed
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:18 instructs the people to keep themselves from the accursed thing lest they make themselves accursed.

questions.question: In Joshua 6, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Compass the city once a day for six days
Shout when the trumpet sounds
Take up the ark of the covenant
Burn the city with fire
questions.correctAnswer: Compass the city once a day for six days
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:3 commands to compass the city once each day for six days before other instructions like shouting or burning the city.

medium.title: Joshua Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Joshua Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What specific command did Joshua give to the people regarding noise before he told them to shout?
options: They were to remain completely silent without any shouting
They could sing quietly but not shout
They could whisper but not shout
They were to shout only when the priests blew the trumpets
questions.correctAnswer: They were to remain completely silent without any shouting
questions.explanation: Joshua commanded the people not to shout nor make any noise with their voice, nor let any word proceed out of their mouth until he gave the command to shout, as stated in Joshua 6:10. This is supported by the instruction in Joshua 6:16 where Joshua finally bids the people to shout.

questions.question: How many times did the Israelites compass the city on the seventh day according to Joshua 6?
options: Seven times
Six times
Once
Five times
questions.correctAnswer: Seven times
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:15 explains that on the seventh day they rose early and compassed the city seven times, which is distinct from the previous six days when they compassed it only once each day (Joshua 6:14).

questions.question: What was the result when the priests blew the trumpets at the seventh compassing of Jericho?
options: The walls of the city fell down flat
The city gates opened by themselves
The enemy fled before the Israelites
The priests were filled with the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: The walls of the city fell down flat
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:16-20 describe that at the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets and Joshua commanded the people to shout, the walls of Jericho fell down flat, enabling the people to enter the city.

questions.question: According to Joshua 6, why was Rahab the harlot spared during the destruction of Jericho?
options: Because she hid the messengers sent to spy out the city
Because she was a friend of Joshua
Because she surrendered herself willingly to Israel
Because she was from another nation
questions.correctAnswer: Because she hid the messengers sent to spy out the city
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:17 and Joshua 6:25 emphasize that Rahab was spared because she hid the messengers that Joshua sent to spy out Jericho, which showed her faith and allegiance to Israel’s God.

questions.question: What warning does Joshua give about the 'accursed thing' in Joshua 6?
options: Do not take any of it, lest you make yourselves accursed and trouble the camp
You may take some as spoils but not all
Only the priests may take it
It must be given as an offering to the king
questions.correctAnswer: Do not take any of it, lest you make yourselves accursed and trouble the camp
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:18 instructs the people to keep themselves from the accursed things, warning that if they take any, they will bring a curse upon themselves and trouble the camp of Israel, highlighting the importance of obedience and holiness.

questions.question: What was done with the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron taken from Jericho?
options: They were consecrated to the LORD and put into the treasury
They were divided among the soldiers
They were melted down and made into idols
They were given as gifts to neighboring tribes
questions.correctAnswer: They were consecrated to the LORD and put into the treasury
questions.explanation: According to Joshua 6:19 and Joshua 6:24, all silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron were sanctified to the LORD and placed in the treasury of the house of the LORD, showing a principle of dedicating spoils to God.

questions.question: How does Joshua 6 teach about the virtue of obedience in the conquest of Jericho?
options: By following detailed instructions from God exactly as given
By acting on personal strategy without God’s commands
By negotiating peace with Jericho’s king
By avoiding the battle entirely
questions.correctAnswer: By following detailed instructions from God exactly as given
questions.explanation: The chapter shows the Israelites obeying God’s precise instructions on marching, trumpet blowing, silence, and shouting (Joshua 6:3-5, 10-16), demonstrating that obedience leads to God’s victory and blessing.

questions.question: True or False: Joshua instructed the people to shout before the priests blew the trumpets on the seventh day.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua commanded the people to be silent until the priests blew the trumpets, and only then to shout (Joshua 6:10, 16). This sequence was important for the miraculous fall of the walls.

questions.question: Which group went before the ark of the LORD as they compassed Jericho?
options: The seven priests bearing trumpets
The armed men
The elders of Israel
The women and children
questions.correctAnswer: The seven priests bearing trumpets
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:8-9 describe that the seven priests with trumpets went before the ark of the LORD while blowing the trumpets, and the armed men went before the priests. This order was maintained during the compassing.

questions.question: What does Joshua 6:11 indicate about the Israelites' actions after compassing the city once on the first day?
options: They returned to camp and lodged there
They set up camp around the city
They immediately attacked the city
They celebrated with a feast
questions.correctAnswer: They returned to camp and lodged there
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:11 states that after compassing the city once, the ark of the LORD came into the camp and the people lodged there, showing disciplined rest and preparation for the following days.

questions.question: How does the chapter illustrate the importance of trusting in God's promises during challenges?
options: By showing Joshua’s faith that the LORD had given Jericho into their hands despite the city’s strong walls
By instructing the people to rely on their weapons and strength alone
By negotiating terms with Jericho’s king
By retreating when the walls did not fall immediately
questions.correctAnswer: By showing Joshua’s faith that the LORD had given Jericho into their hands despite the city’s strong walls
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:2 shows God’s promise to Joshua that He has given Jericho and its king into his hand, and the people’s obedience despite the seemingly impossible walls falling illustrates trust in God’s promise.

questions.question: True or False: According to Joshua 6, Rahab and her whole family were brought out and placed within the camp of Israel.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:23 says that Rahab and her family were brought out and left outside the camp of Israel, indicating respect for camp purity laws and obedience to God’s commands.

questions.question: What curse did Joshua pronounce concerning anyone who would rebuild Jericho in the future?
options: They would lay the foundation with their firstborn and set up the gates with their youngest son
They would be blessed by God
They would become king of the city
They would receive treasures from the treasury
questions.correctAnswer: They would lay the foundation with their firstborn and set up the gates with their youngest son
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:26 pronounces a curse that whoever rebuilds Jericho shall do so at great personal cost—their firstborn would lay the foundation and their youngest son would set up the gates, a heavy judgment discouraging rebuilding.

questions.question: What does Joshua 6:18 imply will happen if the Israelites fail to keep themselves from the accursed things?
options: They will bring a curse upon themselves and trouble the camp of Israel
They will become wealthy and prosperous
They will be given special status among the tribes
They will be forgiven immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They will bring a curse upon themselves and trouble the camp of Israel
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:18 warns that taking any of the accursed things will cause the person to become accursed and bring trouble upon the entire camp, illustrating the communal nature of holiness and obedience.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter shows that God’s presence was with Joshua, resulting in his fame spreading throughout the land.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:27 clearly states that the LORD was with Joshua and that his fame was widely known throughout the country, demonstrating God’s blessing on his leadership.

hard.title: Joshua Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Joshua Chapter 6.

questions.question: What was done with all the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron taken from Jericho?
options: They were divided among the soldiers
They were burned with the city
They were consecrated to the LORD and put into the treasury
They were given to Rahab and her family
questions.correctAnswer: They were consecrated to the LORD and put into the treasury
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:19 states that all silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the LORD and put into the treasury of the LORD.

questions.question: What caused the walls of Jericho to fall down flat?
options: A sudden earthquake
The people shouting after the priests blew the trumpets
A secret infiltration by the Israelites
Fire set by the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: The people shouting after the priests blew the trumpets
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:20 explains that when the priests blew the trumpets and the people shouted with a great shout, the walls fell down flat.

questions.question: According to Joshua 6, who was spared when the city was destroyed?
options: All the priests
Only Rahab the harlot and her household
The king of Jericho
No one was spared
questions.correctAnswer: Only Rahab the harlot and her household
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:17 and 6:25 specify that Rahab the harlot and all that were with her in the house were spared because she hid the messengers.

questions.question: What command did Joshua give regarding the accursed things from Jericho?
options: They should be distributed among the tribes
They should be destroyed by fire
They should be kept from by the Israelites to avoid bringing a curse
They should be sold to other nations
questions.correctAnswer: They should be kept from by the Israelites to avoid bringing a curse
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:18 commands the people to keep themselves from the accursed things lest they bring a curse upon themselves and the camp.

questions.question: Who was instructed to bring Rahab and all that she had out of her house?
options: The priests
The armed men
The two men who had spied out the country
Joshua himself
questions.correctAnswer: The two men who had spied out the country
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:22 directs the two men who spied out the country to go into Rahab's house and bring her and all she had out.

questions.question: What curse did Joshua pronounce concerning the rebuilding of Jericho?
options: The man who rebuilds Jericho will be blessed
The man who rebuilds Jericho will lose his firstborn and youngest son
The city will never be rebuilt
The man who rebuilds Jericho will be king
questions.correctAnswer: The man who rebuilds Jericho will lose his firstborn and youngest son
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:26 states the curse that any man rebuilding Jericho will lay its foundation with his firstborn and set up its gates with his youngest son.

questions.question: How does Joshua 6:27 describe the LORD's relationship with Joshua after the fall of Jericho?
options: The LORD was displeased with Joshua
The LORD was with Joshua and his fame spread throughout the country
Joshua was forgotten by the people
Joshua became king over all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD was with Joshua and his fame spread throughout the country
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:27 says the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is thematically connected with Joshua 6’s account of Jericho’s walls falling through divine intervention?
options: Genesis 1:1
Exodus 14:21-22
Leviticus 19:18
Psalms 23
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 14:21-22
questions.explanation: Exodus 14:21-22 describes God’s miraculous parting of the Red Sea, showing divine intervention in Israel’s deliverance, paralleling Joshua 6’s miraculous fall of Jericho’s walls by God's power.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as "accursed" in Joshua 6:17 and 6:18, and what does it imply in the context of the conquest?
options: Herem — meaning devotion to destruction for God’s exclusive possession
Shalom — meaning peace and wholeness
Chesed — meaning lovingkindness
Melech — meaning king or ruler
questions.correctAnswer: Herem — meaning devotion to destruction for God’s exclusive possession
questions.explanation: The term 'accursed' translates the Hebrew 'herem,' which implies that certain things or persons were devoted to God by destruction or separation, as seen in Joshua 6:17-18.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Joshua 6 to emphasize the completeness of Jericho’s destruction?
options: Chiasmus
Parallelism
Inclusio
Metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: Joshua 6 uses inclusio by beginning and ending the account of Jericho’s fall with the consecration and destruction, framing the narrative to emphasize total destruction (cf. Joshua 6:19 and 6:24).

questions.question: True or False: Joshua instructed the people to shout immediately as they began compassing the city.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:10 commands the people not to shout or make any noise until Joshua tells them to do so.

questions.question: True or False: Rahab’s actions in hiding the spies directly resulted in her and her family being spared during Jericho’s destruction.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:17 and 6:25 confirm Rahab was spared because she hid the messengers sent by Joshua.

questions.question: What was the role of the seven priests during the siege of Jericho as described in Joshua 6?
options: They led the armed men in battle
They bore seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark and blew them
They negotiated with the king of Jericho
They prepared food for the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: They bore seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark and blew them
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:4 and 6:8 describe the seven priests carrying seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark and blowing them as part of the ritual to bring down Jericho’s walls.

questions.question: How does the conquest of Jericho in Joshua 6 foreshadow the New Testament theme of salvation through faith, especially considering Rahab’s story?
options: Rahab’s faith and protection prefigure salvation by faith in Christ
The walls represent sin being impenetrable
The trumpets symbolize the Holy Spirit descending
The priests symbolize the apostles
questions.correctAnswer: Rahab’s faith and protection prefigure salvation by faith in Christ
questions.explanation: Rahab’s faith in hiding the spies and her being spared prefigures salvation by faith, a theme echoed in Hebrews 11:31 and James 2:25, which cite Rahab as an example of faith.

questions.question: Which historical or cultural aspect is reflected in the command to utterly destroy Jericho, including animals, as stated in Joshua 6:21?
options: Ancient Near Eastern practice of herem to dedicate spoils exclusively to God
A command to preserve the city for future habitation
A sign of hospitality to the defeated
A ritual to bring fertility to the land
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient Near Eastern practice of herem to dedicate spoils exclusively to God
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:21 reflects the ancient Near Eastern practice of herem, where total destruction was a form of dedicating the conquered city’s spoils exclusively to God, forbidding personal gain.

theological.title: Joshua Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Joshua Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is primarily demonstrated by God's assurance to Joshua that He has delivered Jericho into Israel's hand?
options: Omnipotence
Omniscience
Sovereignty
Immutability
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:2 shows God's sovereign control over the outcome of the battle by declaring He has given Jericho into Joshua's hand, demonstrating His supreme authority over nations.

questions.question: According to Joshua 6:5, what is the theological significance of the people's shout causing the city wall to fall flat?
options: It reveals the power of human faith alone.
It demonstrates God's power working through obedience and worship.
It shows the effectiveness of military strategy.
It emphasizes the need for human effort in salvation.
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's power working through obedience and worship.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:5 teaches that the shout following the trumpet blast is not mere human effort but God's power acting through the people's obedience and worship to bring down the city walls.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by the command in Joshua 6:18 to keep away from the accursed things to avoid bringing a curse upon Israel's camp?
options: The doctrine of sanctification and obedience
The doctrine of justification by faith
The doctrine of eternal security
The doctrine of predestination
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of sanctification and obedience
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:18 emphasizes sanctification — separation from defilement — illustrating that obedience to God's commands preserves the holiness and blessing of the community.

questions.question: How does the role of the ark of the covenant in Joshua 6:6-9 typologically point to Christ in redemptive history?
options: The ark represents Christ as the presence of God leading His people.
The ark symbolizes Christ's sacrifice on the cross.
The ark prefigures Christ's resurrection.
The ark is a symbol of Christ's priestly intercession only.
questions.correctAnswer: The ark represents Christ as the presence of God leading His people.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:6-9 depict the ark leading the procession, symbolizing Christ who embodies God's presence leading His people to victory and fulfillment of His promises (cf. Hebrews 9:4).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Joshua 6:17 and Joshua 6:19 teach about God's holiness and judgment?
options: God's judgment requires total destruction of all gold and silver.
God's holiness requires separation of the accursed from consecrated items.
God accepts all spoils as offerings without distinction.
God's judgment is arbitrary and without moral reasoning.
questions.correctAnswer: God's holiness requires separation of the accursed from consecrated items.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:17 shows the city and its inhabitants are accursed, while 6:19 sets apart silver and gold as consecrated to the LORD, underscoring God's holiness demands clear separation between what is holy and accursed.

questions.question: How does the preservation of Rahab and her household (Joshua 6:25) illustrate the biblical doctrine of salvation by grace through faith?
options: Rahab was saved because of her noble lineage.
Rahab was saved because she hid the spies, demonstrating faith and God's grace.
Rahab was saved due to her righteousness in works.
Rahab was saved because she was a priestess.
questions.correctAnswer: Rahab was saved because she hid the spies, demonstrating faith and God's grace.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:25 shows Rahab's salvation was based on her faithfulness and God's grace, not her heritage or works, foreshadowing salvation by faith (cf. Hebrews 11:31).

questions.question: What does Joshua 6:26 teach about the consequences of defying God's commands regarding Jericho?
options: The city would be rebuilt with blessings.
The defier would be cursed and face judgment on future generations.
God would forgive the defier if they repented immediately.
The defier would be rewarded for courage.
questions.correctAnswer: The defier would be cursed and face judgment on future generations.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:26 pronounces a curse on anyone who rebuilds Jericho, emphasizing the seriousness of obedience to God's commands and the doctrine of covenantal judgment.

questions.question: How does Joshua 6:27 summarize the theological significance of God's presence with Joshua throughout the conquest?
options: God's presence was limited to the battle of Jericho only.
God's presence ensured Joshua's success and established his fame.
God's presence was irrelevant to Joshua's fame.
God's presence caused fear among the Israelites.
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence ensured Joshua's success and established his fame.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:27 states the LORD was with Joshua, resulting in his renown, illustrating the theological truth that God’s presence grants victory and honors His leaders.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing Joshua 6:3 and Joshua 6:15 about the marching around Jericho?
options: The number of marches was arbitrary and symbolic of human effort.
The repetition of marches shows the importance of patient obedience to God's specific instructions.
The marching was a form of magical ritual.
The marching was unnecessary for the city's fall.
questions.correctAnswer: The repetition of marches shows the importance of patient obedience to God's specific instructions.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:3 commands marching once daily for six days, and 6:15 specifies seven times on the seventh day, teaching patient, precise obedience to God’s directive leads to His miraculous intervention.

questions.question: How does the presence of armed men before the ark and priests blowing trumpets (Joshua 6:9) reflect God's provision of both spiritual and physical victory?
options: It shows reliance solely on human military might.
It symbolizes the cooperation of divine power and human action in conquest.
It indicates the priests were the only ones fighting.
It suggests the ark was a magical weapon.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the cooperation of divine power and human action in conquest.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:9 depicts armed men leading and priests blowing trumpets with the ark in the rear, illustrating God's spiritual presence working alongside human effort for victory.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the fall of Jericho’s walls was a myth and the biblical account is unreliable. What does Joshua 6:20-21 actually teach about the nature of divine intervention in history?
options: It teaches that God can miraculously intervene in history to fulfill His promises.
It teaches that military success is purely due to human strategy.
It denies any supernatural involvement in battles.
It suggests the walls fell due to natural causes only.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God can miraculously intervene in history to fulfill His promises.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:20-21 states the walls fell at the LORD’s command, affirming that God actively intervenes supernaturally in history to accomplish His covenantal purposes (cf. Exodus 14:21-22).

questions.question: What theological meaning can be drawn from Joshua 6:24 about the dedication of spoils to the Lord’s treasury?
options: It shows that all conquered wealth was to be retained by individuals.
It reflects the doctrine of consecration and giving God first place in victory.
It indicates that spoils were to be sold for personal profit.
It suggests the spoils were discarded as useless.
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the doctrine of consecration and giving God first place in victory.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:24 records that silver, gold, and vessels were consecrated to the LORD’s treasury, teaching that victory’s spoils belong to God and must be dedicated to Him as an act of worship.

questions.question: What do Joshua 6:10 and Joshua 6:16 together teach about the relationship between divine timing and human obedience?
options: Obedience should be immediate without waiting for God's instruction.
Human action must be coordinated with God's appointed timing to be effective.
Divine timing is irrelevant if humans act decisively.
Human obedience is not necessary for divine action.
questions.correctAnswer: Human action must be coordinated with God's appointed timing to be effective.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:10 commands silence until the moment to shout, and 6:16 commands the shout at the seventh trumpet blast, illustrating that obedience aligned with divine timing brings about God's purposes.

questions.question: Considering Joshua 6:1 and Joshua 6:11, what theological significance does the strict closing of Jericho and the daily encampment outside the city have?
options: It shows God’s providential control limiting enemy movement and Israel’s organized obedience.
It indicates a lack of faith in God’s power.
It reveals Jericho’s natural defenses alone.
It shows Israel was hesitant to attack.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s providential control limiting enemy movement and Israel’s organized obedience.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:1 records Jericho was tightly shut, and 6:11 shows Israel encamped outside daily, highlighting God’s providence enforcing the siege and Israel’s disciplined obedience in the conquest.

questions.question: What combined theological lesson do Joshua 6:22-23 and Joshua 6:25 teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God shows mercy to the faithful even amid judgment and executes justice on the wicked.
God is arbitrary in His judgment and mercy.
God shows mercy only to Israelites.
God’s justice excludes any mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: God shows mercy to the faithful even amid judgment and executes justice on the wicked.
questions.explanation: Joshua 6:22-23 and 6:25 show Rahab and her family were spared for faithfulness while the city was destroyed, teaching God’s justice punishes sin but His mercy saves the faithful (cf. Romans 9:15).
